I can understand that everyone has their thing that they are interested in but do we really need however many different little subverses? it detracts from the interaction between users and the number of posts for everyone. My example would be science, its all science but there are many parts that could separate into little verses.

What do you think Voat? More is better or consolidation?
Are the subverses too finely divided?

There seems to be an anti mod undercurrent here, especially since many of us came from reddit. Land of the people modding 100+ subs.

We have /v/math, /v/maths and /v/mathematics . They would probably be better if they were merged. I also wonder how deep of a knowledge pool we have here regarding the sciences. From alexa's analytics:

http://www.alexa.com/siteinfo/voat.co

Seems we are above average in some college and college, but below average in grad school. I studied math in college, but I don't feel I can speak intelligently on what most non math people would find interesting: namely distilling down modern research to a level digestible to the average person and explaining why they should care. I would need at least a master's to do that.

From the science perspective I say that the more consolidation, the better.

Not all data is a neat little subset. For example, maybe I have an interest in a specific trading card game, but not trading card games in general. If I'm interested in Yu-Gi-Oh! the trading card game, /v/yugioh is going to be a great resource for me, where /v/tradingcardgames would be pretty much useless if I'm not also into Magic: The Gatering and other TCGs. You could even broaden the definition of Trading Card Game and include general Tabletop Games, at which point the majority of /v/TabletopGames is going to be stuff I have zero interest in.

Now that's the worse case scenario of interests that aren't a neat subset of their more general counterparts. In cases where an interest is a neat subset, like how /v/CoOpGaming is a subset of /v/gaming, it's valuable to me to have a focused discussion on co-op games for one, and a more general discussion on gaming in general in the other. I expect the discussion in /v/CoOpGaming to be focused on co-op, and even if the community is smaller as a result, the fact that it's a subset means most users are probably subscribed to /v/gaming as well.

You're viewing the problem in terms of communities being too small and drawing the focus away from certain subs. In reality, special interest communities are often small anyway and don't benefit from being tossed in with bigger interests. In cases where there's overlap, interested users will be a part of both communities, and uninterested users wouldn't benefit from merging everything together anyway.
Some could be merged. Others are too niche. There's always something that can be improved.

I think there's too many simply by how often I have to keep banning racist and other stupid subverses.

I think there's room for an idea here; a multiverse. Verses that are simply the aggregate of a lot of related subverses.

Hello everyone, and welcome to the first list of new Kickstarter games. This is my first attempt at bringing some fresh content into the verse, and also to help people find new games they might consider backing. How this works: I look through the last week of kickstarter's projects, and I'll list all of them alphabetically, with a link to the kickstarter page, a quick description of the game (as listed by the page) and the lowest price possible to back the game and get a copy of it.

Adapt – The Survival Card Game, by Joshua Long. $20.

Adapt is a highly strategic survival card game where you take on not only the environment, but your closest friends. Players take turns facing challenges on the island, exploring, hunting, and deciding when to betray the other players all while they are hunting down the precious relics to win the game. You can avoid dangerous misadventures by collecting and holding onto the right supplies, like the fanny pack!

Albion’s Legacy – 2nd Edition, by Lynnvander. $60

Albion's Legacy is a a fully cooperative modular-adventure game for 1-4 players (expandable to 6).

In Albion's Legacy, King Arthur and his allies explore Albion in search of specific Realms, while trying to collect enough Quest Coins to win the game! As the Realms are explored, various Enemies will stand in the way, and must be Challenged by rolling the Stones of Chance! Meanwhile, Despair threatens the land! If the Flames of Hope are extinguished, or all Virtue is lost, the kingdom falls! It's up to you to triumph against overwhelming odds!

Blackout: Journey into Darkness, by Richard T. Broadwater. $100 ($95 early bird, less than 50 left)

Blackout is a post-apocalyptic dungeon crawler for 1-5 players. Players take control of 1 or more characters and venture out into the Northern Wastes in search of glory and renown. Blackout is a mission-based leveling system that offers savage combat and rewarding exploration. Blackout is designed for solo, and co-op play, offering 15-20 hours of play.

Character Quest: Heroes (Haunted Oak), by Calvin Nelson. $20. ($17 early bird, less than 50 left.)

A fast-paced dungeon adventure card game for up to 4 people. Takes 20 minutes to play! Try the FREE demo below!

Combat GO! Card game, by Tory Stephens. $12.

Combat GO! is a fast paced, martial arts style, single deck card game for 2-4 players. Quick and easy to learn, suitable for all ages.

Crimson Creek, by Toystorian Enterprises. $12.

Crimson Creek is an homage to 80's slasher films. It is a 2-6 player semi-cooperative pocket horror deduction game that takes 30-45 minutes to play. Where players run to safe locations, peek from hiding places, and search for clues all while trying to survive the blade of The Hatchetman.

Dojo Wars – A Martial World Domination Card Game by Angela Chisrofilou. $54

DW is a card game regarding all martial arts and combat systems developed worldwide from ancient times to the present day.This is Ep.1

Don’t Die! by Abraxus Games. $25 ($5 Print-n-Play version.

Don't Die! is a game of speed, strategy, and a little bit o' luck. Players take turns pulling hazards from the deck, then attempting to avoid it or pass it onto another player. Side Effects on the cards allow you to mess with your opponents die rolls, which can result in some fast paced, card slapping mayhem.

Gilded Devils by Wayfarer Games. $40. ($35 early bird, less than 10 left)

Gilded Devils is a fast paced asymmetrical game of political and entrepreneurial corruption set in America during the heart of the industrial revolution. Half the players will be politicians vying for the presidency during the election of 1872, while the other half are railroad tycoons, building an empire of industry as their rail routes snake across the country, connecting them to lucrative oil refineries and steel mills.

Goat Army by Magnum G. $15 ($10 early bird, less than 50 left)

A strategic and cooperative card game where you challenge your friends to a battle with armoured and crazy goats. NSFW deck available!

Here Be Dragons – A Card Game by Jay Powell. $15.

Here Be Dragons is a high risk, gamble your luck, easy to learn card game. It’s a fantasy game theme where Dragons, Wizards and Monsters roam the earth. It’s up to you to avoid the monsters and find the dragons. Simple and easy to learn!

Hopeless: A Game of Survival by MayVuletichGames. $40.

This game is a great mix of chance and strategy, making it enjoyable for both children and adults. It also creates a different story every time you play, so it can be enjoyed over and over again!

Ingenuity – A game for “clever people by Gal Afik. $25 (comes with Print & Play)

A card game for people who are clever, original, and inventive. Grab a group of friends and force them to play with you!

Kill Doctor Lucky by Cheapass Games. $50.

A new deluxe edition of Kill Doctor Lucky, a classic board game from Cheapass Games.

Kodama: The Tree Spirits by Action Phase Games. $19.

An inTREEguing game for 2-5 players in 45 minutes or less.

Now Everyone Get The F%$# Out! A College Partying Card Game by Starcap Games LLC. $20

Now Everyone Get The F%$# Out! is a fast-paced, screw-your-friends-over party game. You and your fellow players are college students trying to study for a final, but there's a huge dorm hall party happening where you live. To get the partiers out and study, you have to make the other player's rooms more fun than yours, so the partiers will leave your room to check it out. The only way you can study is if every person in your room gets the F%$# Out.

ONUS! Rome vs Carthage and Expansions by Draco Ideas. $17.

ONUS! Rome vs Carthage is a wargame set in the Ancient Era, in where you can recreate some of the epic battles that took place between these powerful empires. The 1st edition has been a bestseller in Spain, leading us to look for funds to produce the English version along with two new expansions:

Prospectus by Mr. B Games. $48.

In Prospectus, players are apprentice-level mages who earn their tower rent by trading potions in the underground Kriztus potion market. Using their powers, they can peer into their crystal balls to predict prices and make their fortunes. But beware! Their prognostication is not perfect, especially when rival wizards cast spells to advance their own agendas!

Scythe by Jamey Stegmaier. $59.

Designed by Jamey Stegmaier (Viticulture & Euphoria) and based on the art and worldbuilding of Jakub Rozalski, Scythe is a 4x game (explore, expand, exploit, exterminate) set in an alternate-history, 1920s Eastern Europe. Scythe tells the stories of 5 factions competing over an unclaimed patch of land surrounding the mysterious Factory.

Sheep Happens – A new strategic card game by Deus Games. $22.

Sheep Happens is a New Strategic Card Game about the endless war between Sheep and Goats.

Tiny Swords by Brian Wolf. $20 ($10 Print and Play)

Tiny Swords is a quick, cute, and chaotic card game that can be played with two or more people. It can be taught and played in only a few minutes, but comes with all kinds of cards and game modes to last you for a long time. You can play anytime, anywhere. You don't even need a table to play!

Universe Game by Diletostra $35.

A space themed board game using marbles dice and discs. Lucky and skillful dexterity is used as you maneuver through the universe.

Werewolf the Party Game: Now with 7 New Character Cards by Matt D'Ambra. $14.

Werewolf is a classic party game for friends and family of all ages to act, bluff, and lie their way to victory.

Zombie Run Board Game by Jakob J. Letkemann. $28.

Easy to play & Fun for all, A family game from ours to yours

Keep in mind, Kickstarter is filled with terrible, terrible board and card games, and my list includes quantity not quality. I do not want to edit the list based off of my personal opinion of a game, or designer, so to keep objectivity, I've listed them all. If I have any comments on games, I'll leave them in the comments, not the bulk of the message. That being said, I have my eye on Crimson Creek, Gilded Devils, and Kill Doctor Lucky.

Scythe will probably be an early purchase for me. I've also never played Werewolf, but would really like to give that a go as well.
